correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the all-field argument. With a,b,c,d,e,f the indicated matrix units, the nonzero products are ab=d, bc=e, ae=dc=f. For any ideal element with a coordinate outside F_q f, one of multiplication by e (on the right), by a and c (on opposite sides), by d (on the left), or by c or a when only d/e remain, isolates a nonzero multiple of f. Scaling the multiplier forces the whole annihilator C=F_q f. All subspaces of C are ideals and all ideals containing C lift from R/C, with C counted just once. In the quotient, T in W=F_q d+F_q e and the projection S into F_q a+F_q b+F_q c determine an ideal up to a linear graph map S→W/T over F_p. A nonzero a or b coordinate requires all of F_q d in T; b or c requires all of F_q e. These conditions are also sufficient. Thus S=0 gives G_{2m}, T=W and S≠0 gives z^{2m}(G_{3m}−1), and either proper T containing one forced line contributes Gaussian counts weighted by p^{(m−r)dim S}. This yields exactly the displayed polynomial, also for p=2 and m=1. Independent coefficient expansion gave [1,3,1,15,35,39,69,87,651,1395,651,63,1] over F4 and total 3011; repeating the one-coordinate count over F4 for scalar-linear ideals gives 59. The brace correspondence follows from lambda-stability giving left multiplication closure, with circle-normality then giving right closure, and conversely by the quotient map for a two-sided ideal.
residual_risks: Original enumeration scripts were inspected, not executed; the general result is proved independently of their output.

value.rationale: This is a complete dimension classification for a natural smallest niltriangular example with nonzero triple products and a substantial distinction between additive and scalar-linear ideals. The classification supplies sizes and multiplicities for every extension degree, with a transparent count of the mixed lifts. The F4 contrast is a useful consequence, not the sole claim.
residual_risks: No claim of a corresponding formula for higher matrix sizes or a classification of all group-normal subgroups.
